scenes.label: Opening Hook
scenes.audio: Ninety-two percent of salespeople have given up by the time the customer is ready to say yes.

scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.audio: Many international sales reports indicate that eighty percent of transactions occur after the fifth contact. But ninety-two percent of salespeople have already given up by the fourth time. There are even forty-eight percent of people who haven't even done the first follow-up.

scenes.label: Problem Solving
scenes.audio: Think about it, it's not that the customer isn't replying to your messages, it's that you've already mentally sentenced them to death. 'Ah, forget it, he probably won't buy, I don't want to bother others.'

scenes.label: Problem Solving
scenes.audio: But have you ever thought, it's not that the customer doesn't want you, it's that you gave up on the customer first.

scenes.label: Real Experience
scenes.audio: When I was leading a team before, there was a newcomer whose performance was always at the bottom. I asked him, how many times have you followed up with your customers? He said mostly once, some twice. I said, then you're not selling, you're testing your luck.

scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.audio: Later, I had him do one thing: contact every customer at least five times before making a judgment. It's not about pushing every time, but giving them something useful each time.

scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.audio: The first time, send an article related to his industry. The second time, share a success case of another customer. The third time, ask him what challenges he's facing recently. The fourth time, offer a small suggestion. The fifth time, officially talk about your product.

scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.audio: Three months later, he went from the bottom to the top ten percent. Seeing follow-up as a bother makes it easy to give up; seeing follow-up as a responsibility makes customers feel at ease.

scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.audio: I'm the speaker, taking you to understand human nature, closing high-value deals. Leave a comment 'Give up', and I'll send you a five-contact action plan table.
